beats.care: It decides whether women get a third of seats before the 2029 election, and how much your state's vote counts.
beats.what: Several outlets report the government may call a special Parliament session late this month to pass the women's reservation and delimitation bills.
beats.why: In April, the constitutional amendment got 298 votes to 230, more yes than no, but short of the two-thirds it needed.

a.body: Redrawing seats now lets the women's quota start sooner, instead of waiting for the 2027 census. Amit Shah said southern states would gain seats, from 129 to 195.
a.label: Government says

b.body: Bring in the 33% women's quota now, without tying it to delimitation. Southern parties fear seats shifting to populous northern states.
b.label: Opposition says

cards.note: No session dates have been officially announced.
cards.title: Link women's quota to new seat maps?

cards.body: It means redrawing constituencies and deciding how many MPs each state gets, based on population. The April bills would have raised the cap from 550 to 850 seats.
cards.title: what is delimitation?

cards.body: PRS projected that a population-based reshuffle could cut Tamil Nadu from 39 to 32 seats and Kerala from 20 to 15, while Uttar Pradesh could go from 80 to 89.
The last Delimitation Commission was set up in 2002 and took until 2008 to finish its orders.

opts: Tie it to new seat maps
cards.q: Women's quota: what's the right move?
Will Parliament meet in a special session by 31 Oct?

opts: It got a majority but not two-thirds
cards.q: Why did the April women's quota bill fail?
cards.why: Changing the Constitution needs a special two-thirds majority, not just more yes votes than no.

hook: 850 MPs and *one-third women*? Why Parliament may meet again

learn.t: How many Lok Sabha seats each state gets is still based on the 1971 census, frozen for over 50 years.

tldr: The Centre may call a special Parliament session this month to try again to pass the women's quota and seat-redrawing bills that failed in April.
watch: Dates aren't announced. Reports say about a week's notice is likely, and a BRICS forum fills Parliament on 26–27 October.
